rejected.title: Neurodiversity
card: Neurodiversity is the idea that human brains develop and work in many different ways. This range is a natural part of the human population.
Autism and ADHD are examples. People with these differences think, learn, focus or communicate in ways that differ from many others.
The neurodiversity view treats these differences as variation, in the same way people vary in height or handedness. It does not treat them as a fault that must be fixed.
A person can still need support, such as changes to how they learn or work. The support helps them take part, and it does not mean their brain is wrong.
rejected.remember: Neurodiversity sees brain differences as natural variation, and support helps people take part.

a.q: Which statement best matches the neurodiversity view of ADHD?
opts: It is a natural variation in how brains develop
It is a fault in a brain that must be corrected
It is a rare behaviour that only affects a few people
It is a result of poor habits learned in childhood
a.why: The neurodiversity view says brains develop in many normal ways, and ADHD is one of them. The option about a fault is tempting, but this view does not treat differences as faults to be fixed.
a.clue: Think about variation, like height or handedness.

b.q: Priya is autistic and finds a noisy open-plan office hard to work in. Her manager gives her a quiet desk. Which view does this best show?
opts: Her brain differs, and support helps her take part
Her brain is faulty, and the desk fixes the fault
Her brain is the same as others, so the desk is a favour
Her difficulty shows she cannot do the job well
b.why: The quiet desk changes the setting so Priya can take part, and it treats her brain as a natural variation. The option about fixing a fault is tempting, but support does not mean the brain is wrong.
b.clue: Does the support change her brain, or the setting around her?

version.title: Neurodiversity
card: Neurodiversity is the idea that human brains develop and work in many different ways, and that this range is a normal part of any population.
Autism and ADHD are examples. Autistic people and people with ADHD may think, learn, focus or communicate differently from most people.
The neurodiversity view treats these differences as natural variation, as people vary in height or handedness, rather than as faults to be cured.
A person may still need support, such as a quieter space or more time. On this view, support changes the setting so the person can take part, not the person's brain.
version.remember: Brain differences are part of normal human variation, and support adjusts the setting around a person.

a.q: Which statement best matches the neurodiversity view of autism?
opts: It is one of many normal ways a brain can develop
It is a fault in the brain that needs to be cured
It is caused by poor habits learned in childhood
It is too rare to count as part of human variation
a.why: The neurodiversity view sees autism as one of the many ways brains develop, part of normal human variation. It does not treat it as a fault to be cured.
a.clue: Think about how people vary in height or handedness.

b.q: Tom has ADHD and finds it hard to focus through long exams. His school gives him short rest breaks. How does the neurodiversity view see this?
opts: The breaks adjust the setting so he can take part
The breaks correct a fault in the way his brain works
The breaks show his brain works like everyone else's
The breaks show he is unable to do well at school
b.why: On the neurodiversity view, support changes the setting so a person can take part, and leaves their brain as it is. The breaks do not fix a fault, because the difference is not seen as a fault.
b.clue: Does the support change Tom's brain, or the setting around him?

a.best: It is one of many normal ways a brain can develop

b.best: The breaks adjust the setting so he can take part

problems.detail: The clue asks whether the support changes Tom's brain or 'the setting around him', and 'setting' appears only in the right option, so the clue all but gives the answer away.

The card frames support adjusting the setting as what happens 'on this view', but the remember line states it as a plain fact, which could suggest all support (for example ADHD medication) only changes the setting. Adding 'on this view' would keep it in line with the card.

check.summary: The facts and both right answers are sound. The clue on question b points straight at the right option's wording, and the remember line drops the card's 'on this view' framing about support.
